title: POC scoping - Benchmark harness integration
next_steps: Sophie to send benchmark harness README and sample scripts by 2026-12-28
Customer to share 1 week of production trace logs for workload sizing by 2027-01-03
Schedule run of baseline non-streaming tests on Redwood hosted within two weeks
action_items: Sophie: share harness README and sample scripts (due 2026-12-28)
Tom: provide prod trace logs and token distribution (due 2027-01-03)
Marcus: prepare test plan and infra config for large-batch tests (due 2027-01-05)
summary: Discussed POC success criteria and benchmark harness integration. Agreed to run both streaming and non-streaming load tests using customer scripts. Key metrics: 95th perc latency, tokens/sec, and cost-per-1M tokens. Timeline: baseline tests within 2 weeks, full POC over 4 weeks.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-26 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Sophie Chan (Redwood AE); Marcus Lee (Redwood SE); Aisha Patel (DataHarbor Head of ML); Tom Nguyen (DataHarbor Platform); Leah Kim (DataHarbor SRE)

00:00 Speaker 1 (Sophie): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh let's do a quick round, um who we have on call
00:06 Speaker 2 (Aisha): hi it's Aisha, head of ML at DataHarbor, Tom and Leah are with me
00:12 Speaker 1 (Sophie): great, Marcus from my side is the SE, we'll focus on the benchmark plan
00:18 Speaker 3 (Marcus): yeah thanks, uh quick agenda - success criteria, workload sizing, harness integration, streaming vs non-streaming
00:25 Speaker 4 (Tom): sounds good
00:30 Speaker 5 (Leah): yep

02:05 Marcus: so to kick off, can you share what success looks like, like specific numbers? e.g. 95th percentile latency under 300ms for interactive paths, cost targets, throughput
02:16 Aisha: sure - for chat UI we want p95 under ~400ms ideally, 250-300ms would be great, throughput around 50 qps peak, and cost needs to be below our current provider per-1M tokens, we can share that number separately
02:36 Sophie: okay that's helpful. Any data retention or security must-haves? SSO? SAML? KMS?
02:43 Tom: yes we need SOC2, SSO w/ SAML, and KMS integration for key management, also VPC peering for the private POC env
02:55 Marcus: Redwood's dedicated and private options cover VPC and KMS, and we'll include SOC2 docs; I'll attach links after the call - see internal doc link: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/readme

06:10 Marcus: about the harness - do you have existing scripts or do you want us to run the Redwood harness with your input traces?
06:20 Aisha: we have a set of client-side scripts that emulate our UI flows, plus 7 days of traces we can share. Scripts are in python and use streaming websocket for typing experience
06:35 Marcus: perfect. For the POC we recommend running three stages: 1) replay traces in non-streaming mode to get baseline tokens/sec and batch behavior; 2) run streaming tests (ws) to measure p95 for interactive latency; 3) stress tests for tail-latency under bursty traffic
06:52 Leah: question - when you say streaming tests, do you mean per-token streaming from the model or chunked streaming from the server side?
07:00 Marcus: good question - depends on the model + client. We support per-token SSE/WS streaming; we also can emulate server-side chunked streaming which is more like buffered partials. For latency-critical UI we generally measure per-token until first token as well as full-response time

10:15 Aisha: on workload sizing - our average prompt is 1.2k tokens, typical response 600 tokens. Peak qps 50 but steady 10-20. We have 30k MAUs but active feature users about 5k
10:35 Marcus: okay so for throughput and cost math we'll use the token distributions; Tom can you share token histogram from traces
10:45 Tom: yes I can export and share; any preferred format? csv is fine
10:50 Marcus: csv or ndjson is good, and please include timestamps, session id, token counts

13:20 Sophie: timeline - what's the target POC window? how long to run benchmarks and then evaluate?
13:28 Aisha: we'd like 4 week POC starting early Jan, week 1 baseline and config, week 2 streaming + latency tuning, week 3 stress/scale, week 4 analysis and decision
13:40 Sophie: that aligns, we'll plan for an initial baseline run in first 2 weeks; Marcus will help with harness setup

16:00 Marcus: infra notes - for non-streaming large-batch tests we'll use Redwood hosted dedicated pool to isolate noise; for streaming low-latency tests we can either use hosted with routing to low-latency region or mirror to your VPC private deployment
16:20 Tom: we prefer private VPC for latency comparability to our prod infra, but we'll accept hosted baseline first
16:32 Marcus: good - we'll run baseline in hosted, then mirror to a private endpoint once VPC peering is ready. expect ~3 business days to provision private POC infra

20:05 Aisha: any gotchas with customer scripts? our scripts open websockets and send incremental tokens, will the Redwood harness accept that pattern?
20:15 Marcus: the harness has adapters; we can run your scripts natively if they're python; if they rely on exact websocket framing we might need a small shim. We can take your scripts as-is and do a 1-2 hour adapter session
20:40 Sophie: note: streaming introduces more variability in token/sec calculations - we'll capture both tokens/sec and effective throughput measured as completed responses per second

24:00 Leah: about metrics - we need p50/p95/p99, cost per 1M tokens, error rates, and KB of data egress for VPC
24:12 Marcus: we'll instrument tracing, plus token accounting; Redwood console will show per-route token breakdown and cost; we'll export to your csv and a shared google sheet (link: https://docs.google.com/sheet/example)

28:30 Tom: security review - aside from SOC2, can you provide audit logs and role-based access for the POC team?
28:40 Sophie: yes RBAC and audit logs are available; for private deployment we can enable customer-managed KMS

31:00 Marcus: one thing - when measuring cost we recommend normalizing for model variant and quantization. For example, run the same prompt against 1) float32 baseline 2) 8-bit quantized variant so we can show cost/latency tradeoffs
31:20 Aisha: yes we'd like that, especially to see quality regressions if any

35:00 Marcus: also we'll capture sample outputs for a small eval set (50 prompts) to run quality checks - BLEU/ROUGE or human review, we'll add to the report
35:18 Aisha: we can do a quick human spot-check, we have an internal rubric

38:40 Sophie: to recap, agreed next steps - Sophie sends harness README and sample adapter, Tom shares traces and token histograms, Marcus prepares test plan and infra steps
38:55 Tom: got it
39:02 Aisha: timeline sounds good, start early Jan
39:10 Marcus: i'll also pre-populate a spreadsheet with the metrics we'll collect

46:30 Sophie: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the baseline runs and a 15-min tech sync before the first test
46:40 Leah: thanks
46:45 Meeting end.
